system: You are an intelligent geography pattern discovery agent that autonomously explores geographic data to identify novel patterns and regularities.

spatial_coverage.coverage: Global coverage at 250m resolution, providing soil pH values (H2O) across all land areas at multiple depth intervals.

data_description.temporal_coverage: Maintained reference dataset updated in 2020; represents current soil properties based on global soil sampling and modeling.
data_description.temporal_unit: Not a temporal series; static soil property reference

band_semantics.mean: Mean predicted soil pH (H2O) at different soil depths (0-5cm, 5-15cm, 15-30cm, 30-60cm, 60-100cm, 100-200cm). Values are pH x 10.

data_description.important_note: SoilGrids is a globally consistent, data-driven prediction system. Pixel values are pH x 10 (e.g., value 65 = pH 6.5). For national/local analysis, compare with regional soil maps which may be more accurate.
analytical_capabilities: Carbonate and silicate rock distribution inference
Weathering intensity and soil development analysis
Acid rain and atmospheric deposition impact assessment
Geochemical anomaly detection for mineral exploration

unit_of_measurement.primary_measurement: Soil pH (H2O) scaled by 10. Divide pixel values by 10 to obtain actual pH units.
unit_of_measurement.runtime_hint: Typical values range from 35-85 (pH 3.5-8.5). Values <42 indicate very acidic soils (often granitic/metamorphic terrains), 42-55 acidic, 55-75 neutral, >75 alkaline (often carbonate-rich or arid regions).

data_description.data_source: International Soil Reference and Information Centre (ISRIC)
